gaps.quote: Each role stream then holds $V/(2W)$ bits (cited).
gaps.note: Spreading V padded bits evenly over W roles gives V/W bits per role; the page never says where the extra factor 2 comes from (e.g. two banks, or half the roles being scratch), so the reader cannot check the stated count or see why the citation applies.

gaps.quote: Frames therefore pass through every gate, linear or not.
gaps.note: The displayed identity is derived only for pointwise linear gates with scalar coefficients, using linearity of the frame; nothing on the page supports the conclusion for gates that are not linear, and the network was described as made of linear steps.

gaps.term: Restoring auxiliary values / roles keep the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: The page opens by saying the network restores every auxiliary value, but its own derivation leaves a scratch role holding $D_{\mathrm{sink}}D_{\mathrm{source}}^{-1}$ applied to its value, which restores it only if that endpoint operator is the identity. The page never says what 'keeps the endpoint operator' means, what undoing the exchange does to the operator, or why scratch values end up unchanged, so the restoration claim cannot be checked.
